claims.claim: The general limit for a lawsuit founded on a written contract is four years.
claims.quote:
Within four years:
(a) An action upon any contract, obligation or liability founded upon an instrument in writing, except as provided in Section 336a;
claims.note: The draft describes a general rule, not a universal deadline.

claims.claim: A credit card agreement is an example of a written contract covered by this rule.
claims.quote: An action upon any contract, obligation or liability founded upon an instrument in writing
claims.note: The statute gives the written-instrument test but does not classify credit card agreements by name.

claims.claim: After four years, the debt is time-barred.
claims.quote: When the period in which an action must be commenced under this section has run, a person shall not bring suit or initiate an arbitration or other legal proceeding to collect the debt. The period in which an action may be commenced under this section shall only be extended pursuant to Section 360.
claims.note: The bar concerns collection proceedings and depends on expiration of the applicable period, not the age of the debt alone.

claims.claim: A limitations defense is available after the period expires.
claims.quote: When the period in which an action must be commenced under this section has run, a person shall not bring suit or initiate an arbitration or other legal proceeding to collect the debt.
claims.note: This establishes a prohibition on filing, but does not describe how a court treats the issue if suit is filed anyway.

claims.claim: The defendant generally must raise the defense in the response.
claims.note: No source on pleading the defense or the timing for raising it was provided.

flags.text: “After that” suggests a cutoff without identifying when the clock starts or accounting for a possible extension under Section 360.
The defense framing omits Section 337(d)’s express prohibition on initiating collection proceedings once the applicable period has run.
“You generally must raise it in your response” directs a litigation step without a supporting procedural source.
A reader could mistake four years from the date of the agreement for the filing cutoff or assume the defense is lost if not raised in the response.

result.summary: Section 337 supports the general four-year limit and the prohibition on filing after expiration. It does not establish a response-stage pleading requirement.
